120084.subject: Chemistry
120084.text: What is the monomer used in the synthesis of neoprene?
120084.sol: Neoprene is formed by the free radical polymerization of chloroprene.

120587.subject: Chemistry
120587.text: Which carbon of glucose is involved in the glycosidic bond formation with fructose in sucrose?
120587.sol: The glycosidic bond in sucrose is formed between C1 of a-D-glucose and C2 of b-D-fructose.

120649.subject: Chemistry
120649.text: Why is sucrose considered a non-reducing sugar?
options: It does not react with water
Its reducing groups are involved in glycosidic bond formation
It is not sweet in taste
120649.sol: The reducing groups of glucose and fructose in sucrose are involved in glycosidic bond formation, making sucrose a non-reducing sugar.

121051.subject: Chemistry
121051.text: Assertion : Glutamine contains amide group. Reason : Isoelectric point of glutamine is 7 .
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false
121051.sol: Glutamine is one of the 20 amino acids. Its side chain is an amide formed by replacing the side chain hydroxyl of glutamic acid with an amine functional group, making it the amide of glutamic acid. In human blood, glutamine is the most abundant free amino acid. The isoelectric point is the pH at which a particular molecule or surface carries no net electrical charge. The isoelectric point ( pH ) of glutamine is 5.65.

121260.subject: Botany
121260.text: One of the most important functions of botanical gardens is that
options: one can observe tropical plants there
they allow ex situ conservation of germplasm
they provide the natural habitat for wild life
they provide a beautiful area for recreation
121260.sol: A Botanical garden is a collection of various types of living plants. Ex situ conservation means conservation of plants or animals in the artificial habitats, which are quite similar to the normal habitats of these organisms. In this way botanical gardens provide ex situ conservation of germplasm.

121535.subject: Botany

121535.sol: When two haploid cells do not fuse immediately, dikaryon is formed.

121942.subject: Botany
121942.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: The Bryophytes include horsetails and ferns . Reason: Pteridophytes are used for commercial purposes.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
121942.sol: The Pteridophytes include horsetails and ferns. Pteridophytes are used for medicinal purposes and as soil binders.

121954.subject: Botany
121954.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Unlike Gymnosperms, the Angiosperms also has naked ovules. Reason: Each embryo sac has three celled egg apparatus - two egg cells and one synergid, three antipodal cells and one polar nuclei.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
121954.sol: Unlike Gymnosperms where the ovules are naked, in the Angiosperms or flowering plants, the pollen grains and ovules are developed in specialised structures called flowers. Each embryo sac has three celled egg apparatus - one egg cell and two synergids, three antipodal cells and two polar nuclei.

122255.subject: Botany
122255.text: What is the class to which ectoparasites belong?
122255.sol: The members of subphylum Vertebrata possess notochord during the embryonic period. The notochord is replaced by a cartilaginous or bony vertebral column in the adultVertebrates have a ventral muscular heart with two, three or four chambers, kidneys for excretion and osmoregulation and paired appendages which may be fins or limbs. All living members of the class Cyclostomata are ectoparasites on some fishes. Cyclostomes have an elongated body bearing 6-15 pairs of gill slits for respiration.Cyclostomes have a suckin

122470.subject: Botany
122470.text: Echinoderms Examples Examples A. Star fish 1. Echinus B. Sea urchin 2. Antedon C. Sea lily 3. Asterias D. Sea cucumber 4. Cucumaria
122470.sol: Asterias is the star fish.Echinus is the sea urchin. Antedon is the sea lily.Cucumaria is the sea cucumber.

122603.text: In which of the following options, all belong to the same group?

122686.subject: Botany
122686.sol: Sea fan is common name of Gorgonia. It belongs to phylum-Coelenterata, class-Anthozoa and order-Gorgonacea.

122783.subject: Botany
122783.text: Select the correct set of examples for the given figure.
122783.sol: When sepals or petals in a whorl just touch one another at the margin, without overlapping, as in Calotropis, it is said to be valvate. Floral Characters of Solanaceae: Calyx: sepals five, united, persistent, valvate aestivation Corolla: petals five, united; valvate aestivation Economic Importance: Many plants belonging to this family are source of food (tomato, brinjal,potato), spice (chilli); medicine (belladonna, ashwagandha); fumigatory (tobacco); ornamentals (petunia).

122964.subject: Botany
122964.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): The placentation in Dianthus and Primrose is called free central. Reason (R): In these plants, the ovules are borne on the central axis and septa are absent in the ovary. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
122964.sol: In Dianthus and Primrose, the placentation is free central. This type of placentation is defined by the condition where the ovules are borne on the central axis and septa are absent. Therefore, both the Assertion and Reason are correct, and the Reason provides the exact anatomical definition that correctly explains the Assertion. Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

123141.subject: Botany
123141.sol: The cotton fibres represent epidermal prolongations of seed coat cells. A raw cotton fibre, on average, gives the following values on analysis : cellulose, 94 % , protein - 1.3 % , pectic substances -0.9 % , ash -1.2 % , wax -0.6 % , sugars -0.3 % and traces of pigments and mineral matter.

123319.subject: Botany
123319.text: Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option: 1. Ground tissues exclude epidermis and vascular bundles 2. Ground tissue in leaves are called mesophyll 3. The root hairs are multicellular elongations of the epidermal cells and help absorb water and minerals from the soil. 4. The trichomes does not help in preventing water loss due to transpiration.
123319.sol: All tissues except epidermis and vascular bundles constitute the ground tissue. It consists of simple tissues such as parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma. The ground tissue consists of thin-walled chloroplast containing cells and is called mesophyll.

123411.subject: Botany
123411.text: The cross-section of a plant material showed the following features when viewed under the microscope. I. The vascular bundles were radially arranged. II. Four xylem strands with exarch condition of protoxylem. To which organ should it be assigned?
123411.sol: In Dicot roots, vascular bundles are radially arranged along with four xylem strands with exarch condition of protoxylem.

123881.subject: Botany
123881.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): In oocytes of some vertebrates, the diplotene stage can last for months or years. Reason (R): The diplotene stage is characterised by the terminalisation of chiasmata and full condensation of chromosomes. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
123881.sol: Assertion (A) is true because in the oocytes of some vertebrates, the diplotene stage is suspended and can last for months or years. Reason (R) is false because the diplotene stage is characterised by the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex and the recognition of X-shaped chiasmata. The terminalisation of chiasmata and full condensation of chromosomes are the characteristic features of the next stage, diakinesis. Therefore, (A) is true but (R) is false. Answer: (A) is true but (R) is false.

123992.subject: Botany
123992.text: Where are ribosomes located in prokaryotic cells?
123992.sol: : In prokaryotes, ribosomes are associated with the plasma membrane of the cell . They are about 15 nm by 20 nm in size and are made of two subunits - 50S and 30S units which when present together form 70S prokaryotic ribosomes. Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis. Several ribosomes may attach to a single mRNA and form a chain called polyribosomes or polysome. The ribosomes of a polysome translate the mRNA into proteins.

124140.subject: Botany
124140.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Fluid mosaic model explains fluidity of cell membrane Reason: Fluid nature of proteins enable lipids to move within the bilayer
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
124140.sol: According to the fluid mosaic model, the quasi-fluid nature of lipid enables lateral movement of proteins within the overall bilayer. This ability to move within the membrane is measured as its fluidity.

124154.subject: Botany
124154.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Golgi apparatus remains in close association with mitochondria Reason: Packaged materials are transported to the mitichondria through the cis face
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
124154.sol: Materials to be packaged in the form of vesicles from the ER fuse with the cis face of the golgi apparatus and move towards the maturing face. This explains, why the golgi apparatus remains in close association with the endoplasmic reticulum.

124290.subject: Botany
124290.text: Which of the following combinations consists entirely of organelles that are excluded from the endomembrane system?
options: Endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex and Vacuoles
124290.sol: The endomembrane system includes the endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, lysosomes, and vacuoles because their functions are coordinated. Since the functions of mitochondria, chloroplasts, and peroxisomes are not coordinated with the components of the endomembrane system, they are not considered part of it. Lysosomes and vacuoles are part of the endomembrane system, making the other options incorrect. Answer: Mitochondria, Chloroplasts and Peroxisomes

124344.subject: Botany
124344.text: When observing the cells of a potato tuber under a microscope, abundant colourless plastids are found. Identify the specific type of plastid present and the primary nutrient it stores.
124344.sol: Plastids are classified based on the type of pigments they contain and the nutrients they store. Leucoplasts are colourless plastids of varied shapes and sizes with stored nutrients. Potato tubers primarily store carbohydrates in the form of starch. The specific leucoplasts that store carbohydrates are called amyloplasts. Therefore, the colourless plastids in potato tuber cells are amyloplasts. Elaioplasts store oils and fats, whereas aleuroplasts store proteins. Answer: Amyloplast - Carbohydrates

124435.subject: Botany
124435.text: Which of the following cell organelles stores hydrolytic enzymes?
124435.sol: Lysosomes are the single membrane bound cell organelles, which contain hydrolytic enzymes. These are also known as suicidal bags.

124582.subject: Botany
124582.text: Which process is enhanced by cytokinins to overcome apical dominance?
124582.sol: Natural cytokinins are synthesised in regions where rapid cell division occurs, for example, root apices, developing shoot buds, young fruits etc. It helps to produce new leaves, chloroplasts in leaves, lateral shoot growth and adventitious shoot formation. Cytokinins help overcome the apical dominance

124999.subject: Botany
124999.text: What role does cytochrome c play in the electron transport chain?
options: It acts as a mobile carrier for transfer of electrons between complex III and IV
124999.sol: Electrons from NADH produced in the mitochondrial matrix during citric acid cycle are oxidized by an NADH dehydrogenase (complex I), and electrons are then transferred to ubiquinone located within the inner membrane. Ubiquinone also receives reducing equivalents via FADH2 (complex II) that is generated during oxidation of succinate in the citric acid cycle. The reduced ubiquinone (ubiquinol) is then oxidized with the transfer of electrons to cytochrome c via cytochrome bc 1 complex (complex III). Cytochrome c is a

125620.subject: Botany
125620.text: Match List I with List II regarding the anatomy and enzymes of C₄ plants: List I List II A. Mesophyll cells of C₄ plants I. Rich in RuBisCO but lack PEPcase B. These plants exhibit Kranz anatomy, which is characterized by large bundle sheath cells that have thick walls impervious to gaseous exchange and lack intercellular spaces (C matches II). The primary CO₂ acceptor in the mesophyll cells of C₄ plants is a 3-carbon molecule, phosphoenolpyruvate or PEP (D matches III). Therefore, the correct

125797.subject: Botany
125797.text: How does a typical microsporangium appear in a transverse section?
125797.sol: The bilobed nature of an anther is very distinct in the transverse section of the anther. The anther is a four-sided (tetragonal) structure consisting of four microsporangia located at the corners, two in each lobe. The microsporangia develop further and become pollen sacs. They extend longitudinally all through the length of an anther and are packed with pollen grains. Structure of microsporangium: In a transverse section, a typical microsporangium appears near circular in outline. It is generally surrounded by fo

125867.subject: Botany
125867.text: What type of pollination do cleistogamous flowers exhibit?
125867.sol: Autogamy: In this type, pollination is achieved within the same flower. Transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of the same flower. lie close to each other so that self-pollination can occur. Some plants such as Viola (common pansy), Oxalis, and Commelina produce two types of flowers – chasmogamous flowers which are similar to flowers of other species with exposed anthers and stigma, and cleistogamous flowers which do not open at all. In such flowers, the anthers and stigma lie close to each other.

125885.subject: Botany
125885.text: How does wind-pollination affect the structure of stamens in flowers?
options: Stamens are enclosed to protect pollen
Stamens are well-exposed to aid in pollen dispersal
Stamens are sticky to retain pollen
125885.sol: Pollination by wind is more common amongst abiotic pollinations. Wind pollination also requires that the pollen grains are light and non-sticky so that they can be transported in wind currents. They often possess well-exposed stamens (so that the pollens are easily dispersed into wind currents, and large often-feathery stigma to easily trap air-borne pollen grains. Wind- pollinated flowers often have a single ovule in each ovary and numerous flowers packed into an inflorescence; a familiar example is the corn cob –

125962.subject: Botany
125962.text: What should be done to observe the various parts of the embryo and the seed?
options: Soak the seeds in water overnight and then split them
Dry the seeds and observe them
125962.sol: Embryo develops at the micropylar end of the embryo sac where the zygote is situated. Most zygotes divide only after certain amount of endosperm is formed. The cylindrical portion below the level of cotyledons is hypocotyl that terminates at its lower end in the radicle or root tip. The root tip is covered with a root cap. Embryos of monocotyledons possess only one cotyledon. In the grass family the cotyledon is called scutellum that is situated towards one side (lateral) of the embryonal axis. At its lower end, th

126103.subject: Botany
126103.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: The egg apparatus consists of one synergid and two egg cells Reason: The synergids have special thin cellular linings which helps to guide the pollen tube into the synergid
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
126103.sol: The egg apparatus consists of two synergids and one egg cell. The synergids have special cellular thickenings at the micropylar tip called filiform apparatus which helps to guide the pollen tube into the synergid

126159.subject: Botany
126159.text: Terms Examples A. False Fruits 1. Citrus B. Polyembryony 2. Astereceae C. Pathenocarpic Fruits 3. Cashew D. Apomixis 4. Banana
126159.sol: Families like grasses and asteraceae undergo apomixis Fruits like strawberry and cashew are called false fruits Banana is an parthenocarpic fruit Fruits like citrus and mango undergo polyembryony

126213.subject: Botany
126213.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): The primary endosperm nucleus (PEN) in angiosperms is triploid ( 3n ). Reason (R): PEN is formed by the process of triple fusion, where a haploid male gamete fuses with two haploid polar nuclei. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
126213.sol: The primary endosperm nucleus (PEN) in angiosperms is indeed triploid ( 3n ), making the Assertion true. This triploid nature is due to the event of triple fusion during double fertilization, where one haploid ( n ) male gamete fuses with two haploid ( n ) polar nuclei (or a diploid secondary nucleus) in the central cell. Thus, the Reason is also true and correctly explains why the PEN is triploid. Therefore, both Assertion and Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. Answer: Both Assertion

126445.subject: Botany
126445.text: What is the acid soluble pool representative of?
options: The entire chemical composition of living tissues or organisms
The chemical composition of living tissue from abundance point of view
The macromolecules from cytoplasm and organelles
126445.sol: The acid soluble pool represents roughly the cytoplasmic composition . The macromolecules from cytoplasm and organelles become the acid insoluble fraction. Together they represent the entire chemical composition of living tissues or organisms. In summary if we represent the chemical composition of living tissue from abundance point of view and arrange them class-wise, we observe that water is the most abundant chemical in living organisms.

126711.subject: Botany
126711.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Malonate inhibits the catalytic activity of the enzyme succinic dehydrogenase. Reason (R): Malonate closely resembles the substrate succinate in its molecular structure. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
126711.sol: Assertion (A) is true because malonate acts as a competitive inhibitor of the enzyme succinic dehydrogenase. Reason (R) is also true and is the correct explanation for (A). In competitive inhibition, the inhibitor closely resembles the substrate in its molecular structure and competes with the substrate for the substrate-binding site of the enzyme. Because malonate structurally resembles succinate, it is able to bind to the active site of succinic dehydrogenase, thereby inhibiting its catalytic activity. Answer: Bo

126860.subject: Botany
126860.text: The figure given below shows the conversion of a substrate into product by an enzyme. In which one of the four options (a-d), the components of reaction labelled as A, B, C and D are identified correctly? array |c|c|c|c|c| & A & B & C & D (a) & Potential energy & Transition state & Activation energy with enzyme & Activation energy without enzyme (b) & Transition energy & Potential energy & Activation energy without e
126860.sol: The amount of energy required to raise the energy of molecules at which chemical reaction can occur is called activation energy. Thus, activation energy is actually the energy required to form the transition state. Enzymes dramatically reduce the activation energy of a reaction, so that most molecules can easily get over the activation energy barrier and quickly turn into product. Simply we can say that activation energy of an enzyme catalysed reaction is lower than that of an uncatalysed reaction.

126965.subject: Botany
126965.text: Dobson units are used to measure thickness of:
126965.sol: The Dobson Unit is a way to describe how much ozone there would be in the column if it were all squeezed into a single layer. The average amount of ozone in the atmosphere is roughly 300 Dobson Units, equivalent to a layer 3 millimetres.

127024.subject: Botany
127024.text: In a cool fired power plant electrostatic precipitators are installed to control emission of:
127024.sol: Electrostatic precipitators are widely used in power plants to remove particulate matter. ESPs work by inducing an electrostatic charge on the particulate matter in the flowing gas and using the forces that arise due to these electrostatic charges to filter out the particulate matter from the gas. The performance of an electrostatic precipitator is dependent on the electrical resistivity and the particle-size distribution. Related Theory Recent years, the increases in toxicsubstances of NO _x and/or SPM (SuspendedP

127292.subject: Botany
127292.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Loss of biodiversity in a region may lead to a decline in plant production, lowered resistance to environmental perturbations, and increased variability in certain ecosystem processes. Reason: The accelerated rates of species extinctions are mainly due to four major causes, referred to as "The Evil Quartet."
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
127292.sol: The Assertion is true as it correctly states that loss of biodiversity in a region can lead to a decline in plant production, lowered resistance to environmental perturbations, and increased variability in certain ecosystem processes. However, the Reason is not the correct explanation because it does not directly address the consequences of biodiversity loss listed in the Assertion. The Reason instead refers to the causes of the accelerated rates of species extinctions.

127358.subject: Botany
127358.text: The one-horned rhinoceros is specific to which of the following sanctuary
127358.sol: The one-horned rhinoceros is specific to Kaziranga.

127368.subject: Botany
127368.text: Which of the below mentioned regions exhibit less seasonal variations?
127368.sol: Tropical regions exhibit less seasonal variations.

127420.subject: Botany
127420.text: Since the origin and diversification of life on Earth, there have been five episodes of mass extinction of species. How is the sixth extinction which is in progress, different from the previous episodes ?
options: The present net species extinction rate is zero.
The current species extinction rate is nearly 10 times faster than that in previous episodes.
The present species extinction rates are 100 to 1000 times faster than in the pre-human times.
The current species extinction rates are far lower than those in previous episodes.
127420.sol: According to the standard biological literature, during the long period since the origin and diversification of life on Earth, there have been five episodes of mass extinction of species. The 'Sixth Extinction' presently in progress is different from the previous episodes primarily in terms of the rate of extinction. The current species extinction rates are estimated to be 100 to 1000 times faster than in the pre-human times, and human activities are responsible for these accelerated rates. Answer: The present spec

127534.subject: Botany
127534.text: The sphere of living matter together with water, air and soil on the surface of earth is called
127534.sol: Biosphere is the biologically inhabited part of earth along with its abiotic or physiochemical components. Biosphere consists of three interacting subdivisions - atmosphere, lithosphere and hydrosphere. Atmosphere is the transparent gaseous mantle surrounding the earth. Lithosphere is the outer solid crust of earth. Hydrosphere is liquid mantle of earth.

127603.subject: Botany
127603.text: What is the major conduit for energy flow in an aquatic ecosystem?
127603.sol: In an aquatic ecosystem, GFC is the major conduit for energy flow . As against this, in a terrestrial ecosystem, a much larger fraction of energy flows through the detritus food chain than through the GFC. Detritus food chain may be connected with the grazing food chain at some levels: some of the organisms of DFC are prey to the GFC animals, and in a natural ecosystem, some animals like cockroaches, crows, etc., are omnivores. These natural interconnection of food chains make it a food web. How would you classify

128580.subject: Zoology
128580.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): The posterior pituitary is often considered not to be a true endocrine gland. Reason (R): It synthesizes oxytocin and vasopressin under the direct neural regulation of the hypothalamus. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
128580.sol: Assertion (A) is correct because the posterior pituitary (neurohypophysis) does not synthesize its own hormones; it only stores and releases hormones into the blood. Therefore, it is functionally an extension of the hypothalamus and is often not considered a true endocrine gland. Reason (R) is incorrect because the posterior pituitary does not synthesize oxytocin and vasopressin. 95298.text: In temperate regions, cambium is less active during the winter season and forms fewer xylary elements that have narrow vessels, this wood is called ____________.
95298.sol: In the spring season, cambium is very active and produces a large number of xylary elements having vessels with wider cavities. 95478.subject: Botany
95478.sol: Molluscs have a shell-like exoskeleton. So, molluscs are also called as shellfish. Bivalves are shellfish with two shells joined by a hinge, examples include Oysters and Mussels. 97688.subject: Botany
97688.sol: Respiration uses oxygen and completely oxidizes organic food mainly carbohydrates (Sugars) to carbon dioxide and water. It, therefore, releases the entire energy available in glucose. It is divided into two phases: Glycolysis and aerobic oxidation of pyruvic acid. Because it takes place in living beings (biological matter) it is called a bio-oxidation process.

97786.subject: Botany
97786.text: In glycolysis, ATP is used in which of the following reactions?

Number of A atoms = 8 1 8 = 1 Since the empirical formula is AB _ 2.5 and the number of A atoms is 1, the effective number of B atoms per unit cell must be 2.5. Let the number of occupied face centers be x . The contribution of an atom at a face center is 1 2 . x 1 2 = 2.5 x = 5 A cubic unit cell has 6 face centers in total.
